title: SVA & Formal Verification Interview Question Bank
description: Interview preparation covering SystemVerilog Assertions, concurrent vs immediate assertions, temporal operators, formal verification, and assumption/constraint methodology.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a concurrent and an immediate assertion?
questions.rubric: Immediate assertions execute procedurally at a point in time like an if-statement. Concurrent assertions are temporal, evaluated over clock cycles, and use sequence/property syntax with |->, |=>.
questions.model_answer: Immediate assertions (assert()) execute procedurally at the point they are reached, like an if-check, using current values. Concurrent assertions (assert property()) are clocked and temporal: at each clocking event they are evaluated in the Observed region on values sampled in the Preponed region (IEEE 1800-2023 §16.5.1), and an attempt can span many cycles using sequence and property operators. Concurrent assertions can express unbounded behavior (e.g. s_eventually); immediate assertions cannot.

questions.prompt: Explain |-> vs |=> in SVA. What is vacuous truth?
questions.rubric: |-> is overlapping implication (consequent starts same cycle as antecedent match). |=> is non-overlapping (consequent starts next cycle). Vacuous truth occurs when antecedent never matches — the property passes trivially.
questions.model_answer: |-> (overlapping): if the antecedent matches at cycle N, the consequent is checked starting at cycle N. |=> (non-overlapping): consequent checked starting at cycle N+1. Equivalent to |-> ##1. Vacuous truth: if the antecedent never matches, the property is trivially true. This is dangerous in formal — you may think a property is proven but the assumption prevents the antecedent from ever firing. Use cover properties to ensure antecedents are reachable.

questions.prompt: You write `assert property (@(posedge clk) req |-> ack)`. The DUT asserts req and ack on the same clock edge. Does it pass?
questions.rubric: Correct: assertions sample pre-edge (Preponed) values; the attempt on the changing edge is vacuous and the check passes on the following edge. Explains |-> vs |=>. Claiming the assertion sees the settled post-NBA value of the same edge is incorrect.
questions.model_answer: It passes, but not on the edge you might think. Concurrent assertions use values sampled in Preponed (§16.5.1). On the edge where the DUT's nonblocking assignments raise req and ack, the assertion sees the old values (req=0), so that attempt is vacuous. On the next edge it samples req=1 and ack=1, and the overlapping implication |-> passes there. The trap is believing assertions see the same-edge NBA results — they never do. If ack should follow req by a cycle, write |=> or |-> ##1 ack.

questions.prompt: A formal tool says your property is proven in 0 seconds. What went wrong?
questions.rubric: Over-constrained assumptions made the antecedent unreachable. The property is vacuously true because the formal engine can never reach a state where the antecedent fires. Must mention using cover properties to verify reachability.
questions.model_answer: An instantaneous proof usually means over-constrained assumptions. The assumptions restrict the state space so severely that the property's antecedent can never fire — so it's vacuously true. Debug: (1) Remove assumptions one at a time. (2) Write cover properties for the antecedent to verify it is reachable. (3) Check if your assumptions contradict each other (creating an empty state space). (4) Use the formal tool's assumption analysis to find dead assumptions.

questions.prompt: Write an SVA property that checks: after req rises, ack must go high within 1 to 4 cycles and stay high for exactly 2 cycles.
questions.rubric: Should use $rose(req) |-> ##[1:4] (ack [*2]) or equivalent. Must handle the range correctly and understand consecutive repetition [*N].

questions.prompt: Design a formal verification strategy for an AXI interconnect. What properties would you prove? What assumptions are needed?
questions.rubric: Properties: no 4KB crossing for INCR bursts, VALID/READY handshake rules and the cross-channel dependencies, no deadlock (liveness), same-ID ordering, response routing through the extended ID. Assumptions: legal master behavior, slaves that eventually respond (fairness), bounded outstanding transactions. Must discuss liveness vs safety.
questions.model_answer: Safety properties: (1) Every INCR burst stays inside one 4KB page: assume it on master ports and assert it on slave ports (a legal WRAP or FIXED burst cannot cross). (2) VALID and its payload stay stable until the handshake, and the cross-channel dependencies hold on every port (IHI0022E A3.3.1; for example, no BVALID before the AW handshake and the last W handshake). (3) WLAST on transfer AxLEN+1, and W data forwarded in the same order as the write addresses, because AXI4 has no write interleaving (A5.4). (4) Each B/R response reaches the master that issued the request: the interconnect extends the ID with port bits on the slave side and strips them on the way back (A5.3.5). (5) Same-ID responses return to a master in issue order. (6) No data corruption in routing. Liveness properties: (7) Every VALID eventually gets READY (s_eventually). (8) No deadlock — every outstanding transaction eventually completes. Assumptions: (9) Masters follow the VALID/READY rules. (10) Slaves eventually respond; these are fairness constraints, and without them no liveness property can be proven. (11) Outstanding transaction count is bounded. (12) No reset during mid-transaction. Strategy: prove safety properties unbounded; prove liveness under the fairness assumptions, or restate it as a bounded-response safety property (every request answered within N cycles) when the design has a latency bound; use abstractions to reduce state space (e.g., data path abstraction).
